newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa business chamber revises down GDP outlook.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa business chamber revises down GDP outlook.

text.p: The South African Chamber of Business (Sacob) said on Wednesday it had revised its growth forecast for 1997 down to two percent from a previous forcecast of 2.5 percent.
The move matches last month's revision of South Africa's growth outlook by the South African Reserve Bank.
"Sacob sees no reason to revise its soft-landing forecast for the economy, although growth prospects are still vulnerable to a number of forces," it said in a statement.

The most important factors governing growth would be the speed with which domestic interest rates declined and the degree of progress in the implementation of the government's Growth, Employment and Redistribution strategy.
The business group said economic conditions were ripe for a cut in official interest rates.
"High interest rates are seen to be restraining the economy, while market sentiment continues to be favourably disposed towards reductions," it said.

"The weakness of the rand is the single most important consideration. While we are not in favour of a permissive monetary policy, business would encourage the Reserve Bank to reduce the Bank rate soon."
The key Bank rate was hiked one percentage point to its current 17 percent level in November 1996.

Sacob director-general Raymond Parsons said Sacob representatives would be presenting the group's arguments for an interest rate cut to South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals at a meeting on August 14.
The central bank governor meets with a number of groups ahead of his annual address, which will be presented on August 26.
"Quite clearly some space has been created for an adjustment to monetary policy," Parsons said.
Stals said late last month that recent inflation and money supply data was encouraging and could pave the way for a rate cut before the end of the year.

Last week, the central bank released data showing money supply growth slowed to a preliminary 12.79 percent rise in June from 15.32 percent in May and bank credit extension growth up 16.39 percent from 16.65 percent in June.

That was followed by data showing annual inflation at a nine-month low of 8.8 percent in June and Customs and Excise data showing South Africa's trade balance swelled to 4.15 billion rand in the same month from 1.75 billion rand in May.
